chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Les Hite as house band at Sebastian's; Armstrong; Hollywood visitors
summary: Royal worked years at Sebastian's Cotton Club, where Bing Crosby and the Gus Arnheim crowd came to hear the band, which backed Louis Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah, Buddy told me that he was hired as a singer.

That was a great band. He sang -- Buddy sang the ballads with the band. He sang pretty good. He was a nice ballad singer, but that was a very good band. So I worked with that band at Sebastian's Cotton Club there for about seven, eight years, as the house band and that's when Bing Crosby and all the guys out of the Gus Arnheim Band and that group, they used to come out when Louis Armstrong was fronting our band. He came out a couple of times, Louis, and that's when he made "Just a Gigolo" and "Stardust," and all of those things of that type of the era.
So you were in that band behind him? (inaudible)?
Yeah, we worked in Sebastian's Cotton

Club there and so naturally, we had the hottest thing in town. So, everytime Bing and that group out at -- Gus Arnheim's band out to the old Coconut Grove, since they'd get off at 12:00, they broke their neck getting out there to see what was actually happening in music out there with us, because we had them standing on their heads out there at Sebastian's Cotton Club for many, many years.
